articles.rephrased_article: Chhagan Bhujbal, a senior Nationalist Congress Party (NCP) leader and Maharashtra minister, criticized the party for not nominating him to the Rajya Sabha despite his longstanding service. articles.rephrased_article: The US and Iran have renewed attacks after temporary truces collapsed, highlighting the region's fragility. articles.title: Can You Die of Sadness? AIIMS Expert Explains 'Broken Heart Syndrome'
articles.rephrased_article: Psychiatrists and medical professionals agree that "dying of sadness" is a complex issue with both psychological and physiological implications.  While intense grief can lead to cardiovascular events, studies have shown a link between prolonged grief and increased mortality risk. The grieving process varies from person to person, but it typically involves emotional pain, changes in sleep and appetite, and difficulty functioning. Prolonged grief disorder is characterized by persistent sadness and impairment, while clinical depression involves negative thinking, low energy, and significant functional impairment.  Most people experience a gradual resolution of grief without professional intervention, but prolonged grief disorder requires psychotherapy and medication.

articles.title: Esha Deol on mother Hema Malini accepting late father Dharmendra's Padma Vibhushan: 'Deeply emotional'
articles.rephrased_article: Esha Deol, daughter of late Bollywood legend Dharmendra, shared her grief over his passing, stating that she misses him every day.  She also expressed her pride in her mother, Hema Malini, accepting the Padma Vibhushan on Dharmendra's behalf, acknowledging the family's wish for him to have received the award earlier in life. Deol emphasized that awards were never important to her father and he valued people's love above all else.  She considers herself fortunate to be the daughter of such iconic figures and hopes to instill their values in her own children.

articles.rephrased_article: Lilian Schmidt, a brand consultant from Zurich, turned to ChatGPT after struggling with her daughter's sleep and found success. articles.rephrased_article: The recent elections in Gilgit-Baltistan, a region Pakistan illegally annexed in 1949, have sparked protests and demands for constitutional change. articles.title: The first spacewalk disaster: How Alexei Leonov nearly became stranded in space during humanity’s most daring mission | - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Alexei Leonov, a Soviet cosmonaut, became the first human to perform an extravehicular activity (EVA) on March 18, 1965, during the Voskhod 2 mission. The mission highlighted the challenges and risks associated with early space travel and led to significant advancements in understanding how humans can work in outer space.

articles.title: Trinamool Rebel, 10 MPs Meet BJP Leaders As Mamata Banerjee Attends INDIA Meet
articles.rephrased_article: Trinamool Congress MPs are reportedly planning to defect from the party after their recent election defeat in West Bengal, with at least 20 of the 41 MPs possibly joining forces with the BJP.  A closed-door meeting between these rebel MPs and BJP leaders is taking place in Delhi, led by Shatabdi Roy, Kakoli Ghosh Dastidar, and others. The rebels aim to form a separate bloc within Parliament and are planning to inform the Speaker of their intentions tomorrow. This internal unrest follows reports of dissent among party members, including some MPs who have switched off their phones or attended meetings with opposing figures.

articles.title: China’s Xi Jinping arrives in North Korea on rare state visit | Xi Jinping News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Xi Jinping, the Chinese President, arrived in Pyongyang for a rare state visit to North Korea. He was welcomed by Kim Jong Un and his wife, Ri Sol Ju. The two leaders are expected to hold a summit during Xi's two-day trip, marking their first meeting since last year's military parade commemorating Japan's surrender.  Xi has emphasized the importance of strengthening ties between China and North Korea, especially in light of Russia's invasion of Ukraine and Pyongyang's recent support for Moscow.

articles.title: Philippines earthquake kills 15, prompts tsunami fears: All to know | Earthquakes News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: A powerful magnitude 7.8 earthquake struck the southern Philippines off the island of Mindanao, prompting tsunami risks in several countries and causing at least 15 deaths. The epicenter was offshore, with tremors felt as far away as Indonesia's Manado city. Philippine President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. ordered an immediate disaster response, including the deployment of military units and the establishment of relief centers. The Philippine Institute of Volcanology and Seismology reported 138 aftershocks, while Malaysia's Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim offered assistance to the Philippines.

articles.title: Lenovo IdeaPad Slim 5x Review: The Best Laptop Under $1,000 | WIRED
articles.rephrased_article: WIRED and Lenovo have released the IdeaPad Slim 5x laptop. The laptop features a 15.3-inch display, 16GB of RAM, and 512GB of storage. It offers good performance for everyday tasks and comes with a fast 120Hz refresh rate.  The laptop also has excellent battery life, lasting over 22 hours on a single charge. The IdeaPad Slim 5x is available for purchase at $850.

articles.title: After Bengal Defeat, Is Mamata Banerjee Preparing For National Politics?
articles.rephrased_article: Mamata Banerjee, after a difficult election in West Bengal, is shifting her political focus to national opposition coordination through the INDIA alliance. This move comes after the 2026 assembly elections and following internal divisions within the Trinamool Congress.  She is actively attending INDIA meetings, seeking to build broader solidarity among opposition parties and position herself as a cooperative participant in the anti-BJP platform rather than a direct leader. The goal is to leverage national issues like unemployment, inflation, and foreign policy to counter the BJP's narrative. This strategy aims to address internal party concerns and regain lost political ground both within West Bengal and nationally.

articles.title: PM Pashinyan’s party wins Armenia election, preliminary results show | Politics News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Nikol Pashinyan’s Civil Contract party won Armenia's parliamentary election with 49.81% of the vote, according to preliminary results from the Central Election Commission.  The victory comes as Pashinyan seeks a mandate to reorient Armenia's geopolitics, distancing itself from Russia and pursuing closer ties with the European Union.  Samvel Karapetyan, leader of the Strong Armenia bloc, came in second with 23.29% of the vote. The election saw over 58% voter turnout, with several opposition parties also clearing the electoral threshold to enter parliament. Pashinyan's victory will likely impact his ongoing efforts to normalize relations with Turkey and Azerbaijan.

articles.title: Kerala Weed Police Raid Man Hid Cannabis Stash In Rice-Filled Pressure Cooker. Then It Whistled
articles.rephrased_article: Kerala police raided a home in Aduppootty based on a tip-off about cannabis storage. After two hours of searching, officers noticed a strong smell from a whistling pressure cooker and discovered 400 grams of cannabis hidden inside. The accused, Bineesh, was arrested and faces charges for possession of the illegal substance.

articles.title: Iran and Israel bomb each other: Is the ceasefire over? | US-Israel war on Iran News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Tensions between Israel and Iran escalated after Israel launched attacks on central and western Iran, following Iranian missile strikes towards northern Israel. The US President, Donald Trump, urged both sides to cease hostilities but the escalation could reshape the conflict's dynamics.  The latest exchange occurred despite a fragile ceasefire established in April, with analysts suggesting it may be linked to ongoing US-Iran negotiations. Hezbollah, an ally of Iran, remains engaged in fighting alongside Israel in Lebanon, adding further complexity to the situation. The potential for escalation and its impact on regional stability remain significant concerns.

articles.title: 3 Air India A320 Aircraft Damaged At Delhi Airport After Strong Winds
articles.rephrased_article: Three Air India A320 aircraft parked at Delhi airport's Terminal 2 were damaged by strong winds during adverse weather conditions on Sunday afternoon. The Directorate General of Civil Aviation (DGCA) launched an investigation into the incident, which involved ground support equipment striking two planes and a third suffering damage from debris. All three aircraft have been grounded for inspection and repairs.

articles.title: KABIL acquires five critical mineral blocks in Argentina - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Khanij Bidesh India Limited (KABIL), a joint venture of National Aluminium Company Ltd. (NALCO) and Hindustan Copper Ltd. (HCL), has secured five critical mineral blocks in Argentina, marking a significant step towards reducing India's heavy reliance on imports.  Union Minister for Coal and Mines G. Kishan Reddy announced the acquisition during a press conference in Hyderabad, emphasizing the importance of securing overseas mineral assets to bolster domestic capabilities and achieve long-term self-reliance. The National Critical Minerals Mission, with an outlay of ₹32,000 crore, aims to strengthen domestic capabilities and achieve long-term self-reliance by addressing India's current dependence on imports for nearly 93% of its critical mineral requirements.

articles.title: Israel iran War Updates Donald Trump Warns Israel, Iran To "Stop Shooting", Then Makes A Ceasefire Claim
articles.rephrased_article: President Donald Trump urged Israel and Iran to cease hostilities, stating both sides are seeking an immediate ceasefire.  He also announced the US Navy blockade on the Strait of Hormuz will remain in place until a final deal is reached. The escalation follows Israeli strikes on Iranian targets and Iranian missile attacks on Israel, escalating tensions after a ceasefire was announced in April.

articles.title: Peru election too close to call with prospect of weeks of uncertainty
articles.rephrased_article: The Peruvian presidential election remains extremely tight, with Roberto Sánchez holding a marginal lead over Keiko Fujimori.  While early tallies by Ipsos show Sánchez leading 50.3% to 49.7%, official results confirm the race is close. Recounts are likely needed to determine the winner, which could take weeks. Both candidates have pledged to address concerns over crime and political instability, with Fujimori promising a tough crackdown on organized crime and Sánchez advocating for sweeping left-wing reforms.

articles.title: Could ex-ISIL fighters be used against Iran, as a Russian official claimed? | Russia-Ukraine war News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Alexander Bortnikov, head of Russia’s Federal Security Service, claimed that Western intelligence services are attempting to utilize former ISIL fighters against Iran. He made the assertion at a meeting of ex-Soviet security officials, alleging that these groups could be used as proxies in the war against Iran. However, analysts have cast doubt on his claims, noting a lack of evidence and potential political motivations behind his statements.  Bortnikov's accusations echo previous allegations about Western interference in former Soviet republics, with some experts suggesting they are part of an information-political strategy aimed at bolstering Russia’s influence within the region.

articles.title: Trinamool Congress Crisis Sharmila Sarkar: "20 Trinamool MPs Forming New Bloc, Will Support NDA": Rebel MP To NDTV
articles.rephrased_article: Kakoli Ghosh Dastidar and 20 other Trinamool Congress MPs plan to join the NDA coalition, formally writing to Speaker Om Birla. The group, led by Ghosh Dastidar as chief whip, will form a separate bloc with Shatabdi Roy as deputy leader. This move follows similar actions in West Bengal where 58 MLAs formed a rival bloc, mirroring the Shiv Sena's strategy.  The decision comes after discussions and is seen as a response to Mamata Banerjee's leadership style and recent party decisions.

articles.title: Messi event case: Calcutta High Court rejects former minister Aroop Biswas’s ‘urgent’ plea for protection from arrest | Legal News - The Indian Express
articles.rephrased_article: The Calcutta High Court rejected former West Bengal sports minister Aroop Biswas's plea for an urgent hearing on protection from arrest in a case related to the Messi visit fiasco.  Biswas was summoned by police after he skipped a Friday summons, and the court ordered him to appear before them on Monday. The complainant, Satadru Dutta, accused Biswas of threatening and extorting passes from him.  The case file was reopened after the BJP took office in the state.
articles.civic_flag_reason: Abuse of power by a former minister is being reported as routine.

articles.title: Trump and Mamdani to cheer on Knicks at first finals home game
articles.rephrased_article: Donald Trump is expected to attend game three of the NBA Finals between the New York Knicks and the San Antonio Spurs at Madison Square Garden on Monday. The Knicks, who are playing in their first finals since 1999, hold a 2-0 lead in the best-of-seven series.  The city is celebrating with heightened security measures, including airport-style screening, due to Trump's attendance and concerns about fan behavior after previous games. Mayor Zohran Mamdani will also attend but in a different section of the stadium.

articles.title: Trinamool rebellion reaches Delhi: 20 party MPs in talks with Union Minister Bhupendra Yadav - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Several Trinamool Congress MPs, including Howrah MP Prasun Banerjee and Bankura MP Anup Chakraborty, held a meeting at Bhupendra Yadav’s residence on June 8th, 2026. The meeting, which included 20 Lok Sabha MPs, aims to form a separate bloc and support the BJP-led NDA government.  The rebellion comes after nearly 60 Trinamool MLAs elected Ritabrata Banerjee as Leader of Opposition, signaling a growing rift within the party. Suvendu Adhikari, who was likely present at the meeting, is emerging as a potential leader of this new bloc.

articles.title: Armenia's pro-West government wins election despite Russian pressure
articles.rephrased_article: Nikol Pashinyan, the Prime Minister of Armenia, and his Civil Contract Party won a crucial election, securing 49.8% of the vote. This victory comes despite mounting economic pressure from Russia, its largest trading partner, and internal divisions over the peace process with Azerbaijan. The election was viewed as a test of Pashinyan's efforts to deepen ties with the West while facing opposition from pro-Russian parties like the Strong Armenia Alliance and the Armenia Alliance.  The results are significant for Armenia's future relationship with both Russia and the European Union.

articles.title: The first spacewalk disaster: How Alexei Leonov nearly became stranded in space during humanity’s most daring mission | - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Alexei Leonov, a Soviet cosmonaut, became the first person to perform an extravehicular activity (EVA) outside a spacecraft on March 18, 1965, aboard Voskhod 2.  While floating in space for about 12 minutes, his Berkut spacesuit expanded significantly due to the vacuum, making movement difficult and preventing him from re-entering the spacecraft. Leonov released oxygen from his suit to alleviate pressure and eventually squeezed back into the capsule, a decision that saved his life despite potential decompression sickness risks. The mission highlighted the dangers of space travel but also provided valuable lessons for future space exploration.

articles.title: Philippines: 32 dead after earthquake off Mindanao coast
articles.rephrased_article: A magnitude-7.8 earthquake struck off the coast of Mindanao island in the southern Philippines, causing at least 32 deaths and over 100 injuries.  President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. has promised that the national government will coordinate disaster response efforts. The quake triggered tsunami alerts in several countries including Japan, Indonesia, and Australia.  The earthquake also caused widespread damage, with buildings collapsing and landslides occurring in various provinces. Authorities have preemptively evacuated 10,000 residents and are working to verify casualty numbers.

articles.title: Tata Steel shares dip over 2% as UK project may face 6-8 month delay amid electricity access issues - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Tata Steel is facing delays in the commissioning of its new 3.2 million-tonne electric arc furnace (EAF) at Port Talbot due to power connection issues. The project, which received £500 million from the UK government, was originally slated for operation by late 2027 or early 2028 but is now expected to be delayed by six months to eight months. Tata Steel is working with National Grid and the Electricity System Operator (ESO) to mitigate the delays and establish revised timelines. The company also confirmed a fire incident at the site on June 3rd, which resulted in no injuries.

articles.title: HFCL shares slip 10% in two sessions after sharp 165% rally in 2026 - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: HFCL, a leading provider of telecom equipment, has experienced significant growth in 2026 driven by strong defense orders and rising demand for optical fiber networks. The company's revenue nearly doubled year-on-year, with EBITDA significantly improving to Rs 315 crore.  However, valuation concerns have emerged as the stock trades at a high price-to-earnings multiple and appears overbought. Recent order inflows from RailTel Corporation of India, a government entity, support the company's strong position in the market. Despite this, some institutional investors are pulling back, suggesting potential short-term volatility.

articles.title: Philippines Earthquake: Watch: Powerful earthquake in Philippines leaves 15 dead, over 200 injured; tsunami warnings in several Asian countries - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: A powerful earthquake measuring 8.1 in magnitude struck the Philippines on Monday, causing at least 15 deaths and over 200 injuries. The German Research Centre for Geosciences (GFZ) initially reported a magnitude of 8.2, but later revised it to 7.8. The quake triggered tsunami warnings, damaging buildings and forcing evacuations in several areas. Rescue operations are underway as authorities assess the damage and provide aid to those affected.

articles.title: Iran Attacks Israel: Watch: Missiles rain across Israel's night sky as Iran launches fresh attacks after two months - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Iran launched missiles at Israel, marking the first escalation since a ceasefire took effect on April 8. The Israeli military intercepted the missiles, but retaliated with strikes against Iranian targets in western and central Iran.  The US President, Donald Trump, urged restraint and reportedly persuaded Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu to hold off on further retaliation.  Tensions heightened following Israel's strike on Lebanon's southern suburbs days earlier, complicating efforts to revive negotiations between Iran and the US. The crisis has impacted regional airspace with closures in Iraq, Syria, and Iran itself.

articles.title: Meta testing Hatch AI assistant as AI race with OpenAI, Anthropic heats up: Report | Technology News - The Indian Express
articles.rephrased_article: Meta is reportedly developing an AI agent called Hatch to compete with rivals like OpenAI and Anthropic. The company is considering a tiered pricing structure for Hatch, positioning it as a premium offering similar to ChatGPT Pro and Claude Max.  Hatch could be integrated into Meta-owned services, potentially reaching billions of users. Meta aims to leverage AI-powered agents like Hatch to generate sustainable revenue streams from its investments in the field.

articles.title: Israel and Iran trade strikes as conflict escalates; IDF hits petrochemical sites in Mahshahr | World News - The Indian Express
articles.rephrased_article: The Indian Express's Global Desk provides authoritative coverage of international developments, focusing on US and Canadian immigration policies. The desk is led by experienced journalists Aniruddha Dhar, Nischai Vats, and Mashkoora Khan, who specialize in global affairs, US politics, and Canada visa/immigration policy respectively.  Their reporting adheres to high editorial standards, relying on official data and sources for accuracy and clarity.

articles.title: Second theft: How scammers use a lost iPhone to steal your identity | Technology News - The Indian Express
articles.rephrased_article: I4C has issued an advisory warning of a new phishing scam targeting Apple users. Perpetrators impersonate Apple Support officials, exploiting victims' urgency to locate or secure their missing devices through fraudulent SMS messages containing phishing links. These messages appear legitimate and redirect users to counterfeit Apple login pages designed to steal Apple ID credentials and one-time passwords (OTP). Once the stolen device is compromised, attackers gain unauthorized access to victims’ accounts and remove the linked Apple IDs from the devices.  The government advisory recommends avoiding clicking links received through SMS or unsolicited messages, verifying website addresses before entering credentials, and using official Apple channels for verification.

articles.title: 525 child rape victims faced pregnancy in 5 years, Allahabad High Court slams ‘systematic denial’ of abortion | Legal News - The Indian Express
articles.rephrased_article: The Allahabad High Court expressed concern over the systemic denial of medical termination services and protections to child rape victims in Uttar Pradesh. The court highlighted that despite a large number of reported cases, only 106 procedures were performed under the Medical Termination of Pregnancy Act between 2013 and 2023.  The court directed the state government to establish functional medical boards, conduct a socio-psychological study on the issue, and create an institutional mechanism for accountability regarding statutory obligations related to child rape victims. The court also recommended exploring a separate legal framework for children born from such pregnancies.
articles.civic_flag_reason: Systematic denial of abortion access to child rape victims is a grave injustice.

articles.title: Iran launches ‘Operation Nasr’, targets 2 Israeli airbases | World News - The Indian Express
articles.rephrased_article: The Iranian Revolutionary Guard (IRGC) launched a retaliatory missile attack on Israeli military bases in response to Israeli strikes on multiple radar sites in three regions of Iran. The IRGC, which confirmed the operation as "Operation Victory" or "Nasr", stated that it targeted strategic air bases at Nevatim and Tel Nof. This escalation follows Israel's attacks on Lebanon, defying a request from the United States to stay out of the conflict.  The recent wave of strikes has threatened renewed war between the two countries.

articles.title: The Art Of Staying Invested: What 20 Years Of Nifty50 Crashes Teach Us
articles.rephrased_article: Indian equity markets have historically shown consistent long-term growth despite experiencing significant shocks, including the Global Financial Crisis, the Eurozone debt scare, the Covid-19 pandemic, and geopolitical uncertainty.  Ajay Kumar Yadav, CFPCM, Group CEO & CIO of Wise Finserv, emphasizes that staying invested through periods of discomfort often leads to greater wealth gains than trying to time the market.  Historical data demonstrates that markets recover after sharp declines, with investors who remained invested during these downturns experiencing significant returns. Anisha Kathotia, an AMFI-registered mutual fund distributor and Founder & CEO of Nico Wealth, highlights that patience is key in investing, as the strongest returns often come after market corrections.

articles.title: Video: Private Jet In Flames During Emergency Landing In Dominican Republic, 2 Dead
articles.rephrased_article: A Gulfstream G200 private jet crashed at La Romana International Airport in the Dominican Republic after an emergency landing attempt due to mechanical issues. The pilot and co-pilot of the aircraft died, while no other passengers or crew members were on board.  The US-registered jet was en route to Austin, Texas when it declared an emergency approximately 16 nautical miles southwest of La Romana. Authorities have opened an investigation into the cause of the crash.

articles.title: INDIA Bloc Meet Live Updates: Pointed Fingers Or Alliance Unity? All Eyes On Delhi Meeting
articles.rephrased_article: 23 opposition parties are expected to meet in Delhi on Monday to discuss their strategy for the upcoming state and national elections. The meeting, called "Janbandhan," will focus on uniting against the BJP and addressing differences between alliance partners.  The Congress, AAP, DMK, and TVK are among the parties expected to attend.  Mamata Banerjee of the TMC is likely to raise concerns about attacks on her party's leaders in Bengal, while John Brittas of the CPI(M) will address alleged political understanding between the Left and the BJP during the Kerala polls.

articles.title: Watch: Khalistanis flags, Indira Gandhi assassination tableau on display at Sikh parade in Canada - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: A float depicting the assassination of former Prime Minister Indira Gandhi was displayed during a Sikh religious procession in Brampton, Canada. S Jaishankar, India's external affairs minister, expressed concern over the display and its potential to promote separatist ideologies.  Jaishankar stated that he believes such displays are driven by political motivations and harmful to inter-community relations.
articles.civic_flag_reason: Display of violence against a former PM normalizes hate and separatism.

articles.title: Meta Layoffs, Mark Zuckerberg Job Cuts AI - Meta Cut 8,000 Jobs. She Kept Hers, But Lost Her Team And Title
articles.rephrased_article: Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg announced a series of layoffs in 2022, citing the need to adapt to the changing landscape of AI. The company has since expanded these cuts, impacting thousands more employees.  While some argue that AI is not solely responsible for job losses, Meta continues to invest heavily in AI development, including hiring top researchers and building data centers. This shift has impacted employees like Meera, who was laid off but remains optimistic about the future of her career within the company.

articles.title: Delhi-NCR Weather Today, 8 June Live: Weather Office Predicts More Rain In Delhi-NCR
articles.rephrased_article: The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has forecast very light to light rainfall, accompanied by thunderstorms and gusty winds of up to 60 kmph for Delhi-NCR on June 11 and 12.  These conditions are expected to bring down the maximum temperature to around 35-37 degrees Celsius on June 12. The southwest monsoon made its onset over Kerala on June 4, three days later than its normal date, but weather experts expect it to advance steadily and cover most parts of the country by the third week of June.  The Regional Meteorological Centre (RMC) has issued a warning for heavy to very heavy rainfall accompanied by thunderstorms, lightning and gusty winds reaching speeds of 40 to 50 kmph in parts of Tamil Nadu, particularly along the Western Ghats, over the next few days. The IMD also reported that rainfall continued at isolated places in Rajasthan with the maximum rain of 93.

articles.title: HFCL shares slip 10% in two sessions after sharp 165% rally in 2026 - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: HFCL, a company experiencing strong growth in the high-speed digital infrastructure market, saw its stock surge nearly 165% in 2026 due to robust defense orders and rising optical fiber demand.  The company's revenue nearly doubled year-on-year, while EBITDA and net profit also improved significantly. RailTel Corporation of India, a Government of India PSU under the Ministry of Railways, recently awarded HFCL a Rs 135.09 crore contract for the maintenance of its data centers supporting Indian defense forces. However, valuation concerns have emerged as the stock trades at a high price-to-earnings multiple and appears overbought.  Despite recent volatility, institutional interest remains selective.

articles.title: US Iran War LIVE Updates: After Israel Strikes, Trump Tells Iram "That's Enough, Come Back For Talks"
articles.rephrased_article: Israel launched airstrikes on Iran in response to missile fire from Tehran, escalating tensions in the region. The attacks targeted central and western Iran, with Iran retaliating by firing missiles at Israeli targets.  The White House did not respond to inquiries about US involvement.  Trump urged Iran to return to negotiations after the strikes.

articles.title: All the Ways Europe Is Ditching American Technology | WIRED
articles.rephrased_article: European governments and companies are accelerating plans to reduce their reliance on US technology firms, driven by concerns over data control, international relationships, and potential access to data under US laws.  The European Commission has launched official long-term plans to decrease dependence on US tech, while the European Parliament switched its default search engine from Google to Qwant. The shift is also reflected in government decisions like the Dutch government's move away from Microsoft Office and Google Docs, as well as the adoption of open-source alternatives.  While these moves are likely a significant step towards digital sovereignty, fully disentangling Europe's technology ecosystem from US firms remains an immense challenge.

articles.title: Doctors Remove Tumour From Woman's Brain As She Watches Pawan Kalyan Film
articles.rephrased_article: Doctors at a private hospital in Guntur successfully removed a brain tumor from a woman, Koteswaramma, during awake brain surgery. The patient remained conscious and watched her favorite actor Pawan Kalyan's film "OG" to stay calm and cooperative throughout the procedure.  The team monitored her speech and motor functions while removing the tumor, which was located near areas of the brain that control speech and movement. The surgery was deemed a success, with no complications reported and Koteswaramma recovering well.

articles.title: IDFC First Bank shares fall after CBI conducts searches, lender shares update on Rs 646 crore fraud case - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: IDFC First Bank shares fell nearly 1% on Monday after the CBI conducted searches at six locations in connection with an alleged fraud case involving government funds. The searches targeted premises linked to senior Haryana cadre public servants and Noida-based Vipam Consultancy Pvt Ltd, as part of an ongoing probe into misappropriation of funds parked with IDFC First Bank and AU Finance Bank.  The CBI investigation revealed evidence suggesting collusion between public servants, bank officials, and third parties in the alleged fraud.

articles.title: Trinamool Rajya Sabha MP Sukhendu Sekhar Roy resigns, says ‘I was unhappy in party’ | Kolkata News - The Indian Express
articles.rephrased_article: Sukhendu Sekhar Roy, a veteran Trinamool Congress leader, resigned from the party and his Rajya Sabha seat citing long-standing internal issues.  He stated he will make a decision about joining another party after introspection. Mamata Banerjee and her nephew, Abhishek Banerjee, are in Delhi for an INDIA opposition bloc meeting following the Trinamool's significant defeat in the West Bengal Assembly election.

articles.title: Falta's 'Pushpa' Jahangir Khan Arrested By Bengal Special Task Force
articles.rephrased_article: Jahangir Khan, a Trinamool strongman, was arrested at the India-Nepal border after being on the radar of law enforcement for alleged threats and election fraud attempts.  Khan had been previously granted interim protection by the Calcutta High Court but it was revoked following the filing of five police cases against him. He had withdrawn from the Falta constituency re-election after allegations of voting machine tampering, branding himself as "Pushpa" in reference to a Telugu action thriller character. Abhishek Banerjee, an MP and close aide of Mamata Banerjee, has been linked to Khan's activities.  Khan’s arrest follows his withdrawal from the election contest shortly before the re-election.

articles.title: Five people injured in stabbing at New York City's Penn Station
articles.rephrased_article: Five people were injured in a stabbing at New York City's Penn Station on Friday evening. Amtrak police apprehended the suspect, who was emotionally disturbed, after a manhunt. The victims suffered injuries ranging from minor to serious and were taken to Bellevue Hospital.  The incident occurred as city officials heightened security measures ahead of President Donald Trump's visit to watch the New York Knicks in the NBA finals on Monday.
